newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE, FEEDER CATTLE END UP, FEEDERS NEAR LIMIT.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE, FEEDER CATTLE END UP, FEEDERS NEAR LIMIT.

text.p: A tepid performance in CBOT corn futures and an oversold condition in CME feeder cattle futures combined to boost feeder cattle futures to near limit gains by the close. Live cattle ended higher on support from a stonger cash market, traders said.
Feeder cattle ended 1.225 to 1.075 cent a lb higher paced by September at 80.200 cents and active October was up 1.175 at 80.825 after climbing as much as 1.400 cent near the close.
Live cattle ended 0.300 to 0.600 higher with August up 0.550 at 66.275 and October up 0.300 at 69.850 cents.
The unexpected lackluster showing in corn futures which closed mixed after limit gains on Tuesday buoyed feeders as did short covering which touched off buy stops, sources noted.

Feeder futures looked oversold after falling four to five cents recently and posting limit losses on Tuesday. General short covering then developed when corn started to slip and strength developed in fed cattle prices.
Breakevens for feeders also turned positive for the first time in months, some sources said.
With corn at around $2.70 a bushel and February live cattle over 73 cents, fall feeders at 79 cents look very appealing, they added.
"This is the first time on paper that it works in five months," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.
R.J. O'Brien, Lind-Waldock, Refco and Cargill Investor Services bought October feeders early and general buy stops pushed prices up late, pit sources said.

Live cattle futures rose on buying sparked by fed cattle trading at $65 per cwt, $1 higher than last week. Expectations also continued that the boxed beef market would be bottoming soon despite further weakness at noon. Demand for Labor Day holiday should firm the market, traders said.
Overhead resistance in back months reflected Friday's upcoming USDA Cattle-On-Feed report. Wide placement estimates on the report made for nervous trade early, they added.

Placement estimates for the major seven states averaged 100.8 percent and ranged from 96 to 106.5 percent of a year ago. On-feed estimates averaged 115.6 and ranged between 114 to 117.8 percent and marketings averaged 105.5 percents and ranged from 103 to 107 percent of a year ago.

RBH, Cargill Investor Services and Rosenthal Collins bought August early with later buying cited by Lind-Waldock, R.J.O'Brien and Smith Barney, traders said. FIMAT Futures USA bought October against selling by RBH and LFG. In live cattle options, commission houses bought October 71 calls.
Volatility was down 1/2 percent, pit sources said.
Boneless beef futures fell on speculative selling following further weakness in cash beef prices. Cash boneless beef fell another $1 per cwt to the $90 to $91 area, sources noted.
Concern over E-coli may have also prompting some nervous selling, one trader said.

U.S. meat processor Hudson Foods Co. is recalling 20,000 lbs of frozen ground beef patties nationwide because the meat may be contaminated with the potentially deadly E.coli 0157:H7 bacteria, USDA announced on Tuesday. USDA learned of the problem after being contacted by authorities in Colorado after several consumers in that state became ill.
Trimmings were also under pressure on reports that warehouses were starting to fill, they added.
Boneless beef futures closed 2.10 to 1.00 cent per lb lower with August off most at 93.40 cents. Trimmings ended 1.10 to 1.50 lower with August off 1.10 at 45.00 cents.
((Jerry Bieszk 312-408-8725))
